specification_compliance: Touch-point audit: the diff reaches frontend/src/components/AppShell.tsx, frontend/src/components/search/useLauncherRows.ts and the new frontend/src/lib/entryVisibility.ts outside the declared list, plus the test files. The spec, INDEX.md and the review records are implicit and not reported.

The code paths for I1, I2, I9 and I10 as written match the spec's UI seams: null means loading and hides every hideable entry; a set removes its keys; a failed or 500 response settles to the empty set; the hook keeps the answer tied to its drive.
Per the touch-point audit, the endpoint, schema, admin path, docs and hook are in the declared list; I did not check them against behaviour beyond reading.
potential_unspecified_behavior: When useCurrentDrive() returns null, useEntryVisibility returns the empty set (not null), so the sidebar would draw built-in rows at once; the spec does not say what the sidebar shows without a drive. No user-visible effect was found because no built-in row is drawn without a drive.
regression_risks: Three separate visibility fetches per page (AppShell, DriveHome, useLauncherRows) each draw their own loading state; a change to one caller could desynchronise the sidebar, Home row and palette.
test_coverage: The new tests cover the listed states (loading, failed, I2, I4, I5, I10, I11) for each named surface.
Not covered by any test I found: AppShell's wiring of hiddenKeys into Sidebar, and useLauncherRows' wiring of hiddenKeys into the palette. Both are reached only through the untested composition.
